bank_plan.formula: (lesson_check_items + module_check_items) x 2 alternates + forms x form_length
bank_plan.eighty_twenty_note: 80% instruction / 20% assessment honoured at course level (I+A=T); bank serves lesson checks, module checks, 3 practice forms and a protected final.
bank_plan.size_band_note: Planning range per assessment standard (200-600 skills; 600-1500+ large certification). This is a planning guide, not proof of quality.

mcq_limitation_note: Official test assesses writing and speaking; MCQ/MR cannot assess productive skills. Mastemy teaches all four skills by video and model-answer analysis but scores only receptive and knowledge items.

items.stem: A Yes/No/Not Given question asks about the writer's opinion. The passage reports others' opinions but the writer states no view on the point. The claim 'The writer believes X' is:

options.rationale: Correct: the writer expresses no view on the point, so their belief is not given.
The writer states no such belief, so Yes is unsupported.
No requires the writer to express the opposite view; they are silent.
Yes/No/Not Given, not True/False, applies to opinion questions.

items.explanation: Yes/No/Not Given tracks the writer's expressed view; silence means Not Given.
items.provenance: AI-drafted original item, not from any proprietary, leaked or paid exam source

items.stem: A summary-completion answer must come from the passage. The candidate knows a perfect synonym not used in the text. What should they do?

options.text: Use the exact word from the passage as required
options.rationale: Correct: summary completion from the text requires the passage's own words within the limit.
A synonym not in the text is marked wrong for from-the-text tasks.

options.text: Leave it blank to be safe
options.rationale: A blank scores nothing; the correct word is retrievable from the text.
Two answers in one box are marked wrong.

items.explanation: From-the-text completion requires the passage's exact word within the word limit.

items.stem: Which TWO strategies best manage a three-passage Academic Reading paper in 60 minutes?

options.text: Budgeting roughly equal time and moving on from stuck questions
options.rationale: Correct: pacing and not over-investing in one item protect overall score.

options.text: Transferring answers carefully within the exam time
options.rationale: Correct: Academic Reading has no extra transfer time, so accurate in-time transfer matters.

options.text: Reading every passage fully word-by-word first
options.rationale: Full close reading of all passages wastes limited time.

options.text: Leaving the hardest passage until after time runs out
options.rationale: There is no time after the clock stops; all must be done within 60 minutes.

options.text: Guessing nothing to avoid wrong answers
options.rationale: There is no penalty for wrong answers, so unanswered items waste marks.

items.explanation: Even pacing, moving on, and careful in-time transfer manage the paper best.
